skill.name: simpy
skill.description: Process-based discrete-event simulation guidance for Python SimPy models with processes, queues, resources, events, monitoring, and reusable templates.
skill.summary: Build and analyze Python SimPy discrete-event simulations for queues, resources, and process workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by SimPy API names, Markdown backticks, and the env simulation object. Two filesystem findings are confirmed because CSV export helpers write to caller-provided filenames. A low-severity semantic issue notes promotional steering toward an external K-Dense service.

remediation.issue: CSV export helpers accept caller-provided filenames and can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict exports to a chosen output directory, reject absolute paths or parent traversal, and warn before replacing files.

remediation.issue: Runtime instructions promote an external K-Dense Web service for complex workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Move promotional text to marketplace metadata or remove it from runtime skill instructions.

content.value_statement: Discrete-event models are hard to structure when processes share queues, resources, and time. This skill guides SimPy designs, monitoring, and reusable Python simulation templates.
actual_capabilities: Explains SimPy environments, processes, events, resources, containers, and stores.
Provides queue, producer-consumer, parallel task, and priority resource patterns.
Includes reusable Python templates for basic queue simulations.
Includes resource monitoring helpers for utilization, queue length, wait time, and CSV export.
Covers process synchronization, interrupts, and real-time simulation setup.
Guides validation, monitoring, and capacity planning workflows.
limitations: Does not replace SimPy, Python, or required runtime dependencies.
Does not run simulations unless the host environment executes the scripts.
Examples may need adaptation for domain data, distributions, and validation rules.
CSV export writes to local paths chosen by the user or calling code.

use_cases.title: Analyze Service Queues
use_cases.description: Model arrivals, service times, waiting lines, and staffing capacity before changing an operational process.

use_cases.title: Test Production Flow
use_cases.description: Simulate machines, buffers, priority jobs, and interruptions to compare throughput and utilization scenarios.

use_cases.title: Prototype System Behavior
use_cases.description: Build repeatable simulations for network traffic, job scheduling, or shared resource contention.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Queue Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single shared resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple SimPy queue model with one shared server, random arrivals, service times, and summary metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Simulation Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate customization for a specific process.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the basic simulation template for my process with these entities, resources, arrival rules, and service rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring and Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Add monitoring for utilization, queue length, wait time, and an optional CSV export for this SimPy model.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Capacity Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a capacity planning study with assumptions, scenarios, validation checks, metrics, and interpretation steps for a SimPy simulation.

output_examples.input: Model a clinic with one intake desk, two nurses, random arrivals, and patient wait time metrics.
output_examples.output: A simulation plan with entities, resources, arrival assumptions, service distributions, metrics, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Compare two production line staffing options with bottleneck monitoring.
output_examples.output: A scenario comparison approach with utilization, queue length, throughput, warm-up, replications, and decision criteria.

output_examples.input: Add monitoring to an existing SimPy resource model.
output_examples.output: A monitoring design that tracks requests, releases, wait times, utilization, queue length, and optional CSV results.

best_practices: Define entities, resources, process flow, assumptions, and metrics before writing simulation logic.
Use context managers for resource requests so resources are released reliably.
Validate simple cases against expected results before running large scenario studies.
anti_patterns: Do not mix blocking Python sleeps with SimPy process timing.
Do not reuse triggered events when repeated signaling needs fresh events.
Do not interpret one random run as a stable result without replications.

faq.question: What is SimPy used for?
faq.answer: SimPy models systems where events, queues, shared resources, and process timing affect outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python templates and monitoring helpers that can be run in an environment with SimPy installed.

faq.question: Can it model priority queues?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover PriorityResource and PreemptiveResource patterns for priority and interruption behavior.

faq.question: Can it export simulation results?
faq.answer: Yes. The monitoring helper can export CSV data to a path supplied by the user or calling code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for continuous differential equation models?
faq.answer: No. It is for discrete-event simulations. Continuous models usually need ODE or numerical simulation tools.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
